scope: Eight teaching targets: four B targets with five new SVGs, four C targets with one new SVG and three exact reviewed B assets reused.

sourceReview.chapter15: Previously read full deck and native extraembryonic/development figures; additional native neurulation image c444533b and birth-positive-feedback image 50e5e5ef inspected. The latter shows feedback, not the three birth stages.
correctedSourceClaims: Meiosis I products do not necessarily contain an entirely maternal or entirely paternal chromosome set.
No intervening S phase does not mean every possible interkinesis event is absent.
Meiosis II products are not universally genetically identical; prior crossing over can distinguish sisters.
Haploid nuclei, spermatids and mature functional gametes are distinct outcomes.

nativeReview: All six newly selected final SVGs inspected. Existing B asset reviews reused without regeneration. Birth v2 oxygen labels remove exchange-arrow ambiguity.
comparisonProcess: Batch side-by-side gallery sections prepared from inspected native source/current figures and selected original SVGs. No claim that every rendered gallery section was separately re-inspected.

priorReview.finding: Native2n=4 symbolic set model has two long/two short unduplicated chromosomes, the same four duplicated chromosomes, then one long/one short duplicated in one meiotic-I product. Human count row46/46,46/92,23/46 matches chromosomes/DNA molecules per cell; picture and human counts are explicitly distinct.

One→two→four cell inventory and46 duplicated→23 duplicated→23 unduplicated per-cell counts verified. v2 moves tree right to separate labels from circles. Differentiation does not halve counts; no replication between divisions.

Prophase-I prenatal and metaphase-II ovulatory pauses,46 duplicated→23 duplicated→23 unduplicated maternal counts, and unequal polar-body branches verified. v2 routes both branches clear of text. Final count excludes sperm; no three-polar-body inevitability or completed meiosis at ovulation.

bindings.finding: Approximate post-fertilization and obstetric ages stay distinct. The embryonic/fetal distinction and overlapping trimester patterns accompany a schematic plate-to-groove-to-tube sequence; closure varies across time and position. These are explanatory models, not clinical schedules or microscopic observations.

Fictional qualitative groups differ in both agent exposure and culture temperature. Their marker difference cannot isolate a single cause. This separate example does not alter the required four-count investigation dataset or supply its answer graph.

Dilation, delivery and placental delivery are broad events. Oxygen arrows distinguish placental exchange between distinct bloodstreams from newborn lung exchange. Effective ventilation and circulatory adaptation are required; the illustration does not show maternal blood flowing into fetal blood.

Barrier, hormonal, transport and outside-body fertilization mechanisms have different targets. Mechanism alone does not guarantee pregnancy outcomes. Denominator, time interval and five perspectives remain explicit; no personal recommendation or ranking of families.

Exact reviewed B asset reused for the same chromosome-count distinction. Its picture uses 2n=4 and its separately labelled human row uses 2n=46; C prose also supplies a distinct 2n=8 worked example. These examples must not be conflated. Replication changes DNA copies without doubling ploidy.

The 2n=4 starting cell has four duplicated chromosomes. Each product after meiosis I has two duplicated chromosomes and one homologous set. Counts refer to the outlined products, not an undivided anaphase cell. Long/short marks denote types and colours distinguish homologues; crossing over is explicitly omitted.

The same count model continues meiosis I products through sister separation to four haploid products with two unduplicated chromosomes each. There is no intervening S phase. Crossing over is omitted in this model, so its matching final symbols must not imply that actual meiosis II products are always genetically identical or four equally functional gametes.

Exact reviewed B models compare four similarly sized spermatids followed by differentiation with unequal oocyte divisions, prenatal prophase I arrest and ovulatory metaphase II arrest. The final oocyte-panel chromosome count is maternal only. Final haploid nuclei and functional gametes are not interchangeable counts.
